Title: Foreigner nabbed for breaking auxiliary cop's teeth, damaging Genting casino
Article:
KUANTAN: A foreigner was arrested for allegedly injuring an auxiliary policeman and damaging casino equipment at Sky Casino in Genting Highlands yesterday.
Acting Bentong police chief Deputy Superintendent Azmi Mahmod said preliminary investigations revealed that the 34-year-old man, believed to have been drunk, had behaved aggressively towards members of the public before entering the casino.
He said the man then damaged the screens of three gambling machines by repeatedly banging his head against them, as well as two chairs, resulting in estimated losses of RM85,000.
"The man sustained a forehead injury that required six stitches," he said in a statement.
Azmi said the man also allegedly punched a 32-year-old auxiliary policeman in the mouth, breaking two of his teeth.
He said the policeman had since received treatment at Bentong Hospital.
Initial checks revealed that the man had no criminal record, he said, adding that the foreigner tested negative for drugs.
The case is being investigated under Sections 323 and 427 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt and committing mischief resulting in property damage, respectively.
The first carries a jail term of up to a year, or a fine or both upon conviction, while the second can lead to between one and five years' jail or fine, or both.

Title: [UPDATED] BN, PN ink pact to face 16th Melaka election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional and its strategic partner Pas, representing parties under Perikatan Nasional, today formalised their cooperation and political understanding ahead of the 16th Melaka election.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed this evening by him and PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan, who is also Pas secretary-general.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi witnessed the signing.
"The Umno Supreme Council, which met today, unanimously agreed to formalise cooperation and a political understanding with strategic partners Pas and other parties under PN to face the Melaka election," he told reporters after the council meeting at Menara Dato Onn.
Asyraf said the supreme council had also agreed that BN and PN would launch a joint election manifesto, pledging to provide the best services to the people and build on the achievements in public service delivery and state development under the previous Melaka state government.
"The manifesto will be launched in the evening after nomination day (on Saturday). If there are any changes, we will inform later," he said.
He added that the party's election machinery and supporters would be directed to assist and provide strong support to all PN candidates contesting in the election.
"The supreme council also called on party leaders and election machinery to conduct their campaigns prudently and ethically, without resorting to slander, ridicule or insults against opposing parties," he said.
Asked whether Parti Wawasan would also field their candidates, Asyraf said the matter should be referred to PN.
"That is for PN to decide. We leave it to them to determine the candidates and the parties that will contest the seven state seats, as agreed upon under the terms of the agreement and understanding reached with BN.
"BN will contest 21 seats, including two allocated to MCA and one to MIC, while PN will contest seven seats," he said.
Meanwhile, BN Melaka chairman and caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said the meeting discussed the coordination of campaign activities for the state election, with clear instructions for everyone to focus on the 21 constituencies being contested.
"Every vote counts in our efforts to defend all 21 constituencies," he said.
The Election Commission has set polling day for Nov 14, with early voting on Nov 10.
In the 2021 Melaka election, BN won 21 of the 28 seats contested, enabling it to form the state government. Pakatan Harapan won five seats, while PN secured two.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No confirmation of Malaysians affected by Spain train collision, embassy contacts authorities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian embassy in Madrid has yet to receive confirmation of any Malaysians affected by a collision involving two high-speed passenger trains near Urda in Toledo, Spain.
The Foreign Ministry said it was closely monitoring the situation through the embassy following the collision, which occurred at approximately 8.54am local time.
"The embassy is in contact with the relevant Spanish authorities and railway operators to ascertain whether any Malaysians were among the passengers involved and to coordinate consular assistance should the need arise," the ministry said in a media advisory.
It added that high-speed rail services between Madrid and Andalusia had reportedly been suspended following the incident.
The ministry advised Malaysians travelling in Spain, particularly those planning to use the affected railway services, to check the latest service updates directly with their respective operators and make alternative travel arrangements where necessary.
It also urged Malaysians who may have been affected by the incident, or anyone with information concerning Malaysians who may have been involved, to contact the embassy to assist with verification and the provision of consular assistance.
Malaysians residing in or travelling to Spain have been encouraged to register and regularly update their contact details via the e-Konsular portal at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my (https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my/).
For immediate consular assistance or emergencies, the ministry said Malaysian citizens could contact the Malaysian Embassy in Madrid through its 24-hour emergency helpline at +34 659894943, general enquiry lines at +34 915550684 or +34 915550737, or via email at mwmadrid@kln.gov.my.
The ministry said it would continue to monitor developments closely and provide further updates as necessary.

Title: Cops detain three, seize 376.2kg of pangolin scales in Negri Sembilan
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police detained three men and seized 376.2kg of pangolin scales worth an estimated RM376,200 in an integrated operation at a premises in Negri Sembilan yesterday.
The operation, which began at 12.30pm, was carried out by the Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence Division of Bukit Aman's Internal Security and Public Order Department, in collaboration with the Wildlife and National Parks Department (Perhilitan), under Op Bersepadu Khazanah (OBK).
In a statement today, division commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said police found 15 boxes of pangolin scales during a search of the premises.
"Other items seized during the operation included nine mobile phones of various brands, a weighing scale and a padlock.
"The total value of the seizure, including other items, is estimated at RM401,700," he said, adding that police took all suspects and seized items to the Nilai police headquarters before handing them over to Perhilitan investigators for further action.
Zaki said the case was being investigated under Section 68 of the Wildlife Conservation Act 2010 (Act 716), relating to offences involving wildlife, its parts or derivatives.
"This large-scale seizure underscores the importance of continued intelligence and enforcement operations to combat networks involved in storing, collecting and distributing products derived from wildlife," he said.
Zaki said the division had carried out 288 raids nationwide between Jan 1 and today, involving various offences, including wildlife smuggling, untaxed goods, leakage of controlled and subsidised goods, and e-waste-related activities that resulted in 471 arrests, with the total value of seizures estimated at RM350.35 million.
He said 66 cases were recorded this year, involving 74 arrests and seizures worth an estimated RM99.70 million under the OBK.

Title: A-GC: Financial crime investigation reports presented to cabinet before public disclosure
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Reports arising from investigations by the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) Special Investigation Committee on Financial Crime Issues will be presented to the cabinet for consideration and action before being made public.
In a statement today, the A-GC said the committee had been mandated to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the trail of financial crimes from their earliest stages.
"The investigation will be conducted transparently and comprehensively, without being limited to any particular individual or company, to ensure that all relevant aspects are thoroughly examined based on the facts and evidence obtained," it said.
The committee held its first meeting today, chaired by Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, to determine its membership, as well as the scope and parameters of the investigation, the A-GC said.
The meeting was attended by representatives from the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission, police, Inland Revenue Board, Bank Negara Malaysia, Securities Commission Malaysia and the National Anti-Financial Crime Centre.
The A-GC said investigations would involve cooperation among the relevant enforcement agencies to ensure coordinated and integrated action.
On Oct 20, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced in the Dewan Rakyat that the A-GC had been mandated to lead and coordinate several high-profile financial crime investigations.
Anwar gave an assurance that the government would not protect any party involved in corporate criminal activities.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Buried alive: Baby in critical condition in Kapit
Article:
KAPIT: A newborn baby boy was found buried alive near a rented house in Jalan Airport, here, yesterday.
District police chief Deputy Superintendent Rohana Nanu said the baby was found by policemen who heard its while conducting a search in the area about 2.30pm.
"The baby boy was found by the police during a search at the scene after hearing the cries of the baby. The newborn was found buried," she said when contacted today.
Rohana said the baby was in critical condition and was sent to Sibu Hospital for further treatment.
She added that a female suspect has been identified, but her statement has not yet been recorded as she is still receiving treatment at the hospital.
The case is being investigated under Section 317 of the Penal Code for exposure and abandonment of a child by a parent or person in whose care the child has been placed, which carries a jail term of up to seven years, a fine or both, upon conviction.

Title: Oriental interest terminates proposed acquisition of Chin Hin Jitra and CHJ Motor
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Property developer Oriental Interest Bhd will not proceed with the proposed RM280 million acquisition of the entire equity interest in Chin Hin (Jitra) Sdn Bhd and CHJ Motor Holdings Sdn Bhd.
In a Bursa Malaysia filing today, Oriental Interest said the company and the vendor, LLSB 1980 Holdings Sdn Bhd, had mutually agreed to terminate, revoke and rescind the conditional share sale and purchase agreement through a termination agreement dated Oct 28, 2026.
It added that the decision followed a reassessment of the company's business strategies, diversification considerations and the strategic alignment of the proposed acquisitions with its overall business objectives.
"Among other factors, the company took into consideration the longer than anticipated timeframe and additional resources required to fulfil the relevant regulatory, approval and procedural requirements for completion," said Oriental Interest.
Following the termination, the company said neither party would have any claims against the other arising from the agreement.
"Oriental Interest, through its subsidiaries, remains focused on growing its core property development and general construction businesses, supported by a healthy pipeline of ongoing developments, growing unbilled sales and a sizeable landbank," it added.
To date, Oriental Interest's landbank stood at approximately 814.63 hectares of strategically located development land, providing a strong foundation for future projects and long-term earnings visibility.

Title: Lawyers want restraint in disciplinary action against Shuhaily
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The authorities should exercise restraint before making any decision on Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain's tenure as Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general.
Shuhaily's lawyer, Datuk Baljit Singh Sidhu, said the charge against his client under Section 323 of the Penal Code should be considered in its proper legal context, stressing that the principle of innocent until proven guilty must remain paramount.
He said the offence was non-seizable, ordinarily dealt with as a summons case, as well as being bailable.
He added that it was not a registrable offence under the Registration of Criminals and Undesirable Persons Act 1969.
"Any decision affecting his tenure should be made objectively, with due consideration of the law, the facts and the circumstances of the case," he said.
Baljit also said public sentiment had been overwhelmingly supportive of the work Shuhaily had undertaken so far.
"Under the circumstances, I would urge that we exercise sound judgment, restraint and circumspection before taking any position or making any representation to His Majesty the King.
"The matter deserves careful and responsible consideration," he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, a senior lawyer familiar with the case said any disciplinary action should be proportionate to the alleged offence and supported by clear reasons.
The lawyer, who declined to be named, said the charge was a minor, non-seizable, bailable and compoundable offence under the Criminal Procedure Code (CPC).
He said suspending or interdicting Shuhaily under the Public Officers (Conduct and Discipline) Regulations 1993 before the court process concluded could be disproportionate.
"Section 260 of the CPC expressly allows offences of this nature to be settled through a compound, which operates in law as an acquittal.
"Any aggressive disciplinary action at this stage circumvents this statutory framework and penalises an officer on the presumption of guilt for a matter the law permits to be resolved externally," he said.
He warned that an unreasonable suspension could be challenged through a judicial review in the High Court, potentially exposing the authorities to legal costs and claims for aggravated damages.
"The legally sound course of action is for the authorities to exercise administrative restraint and allow the judicial process to take its course to avoid hasty action that could trigger costly and embarrassing litigation against the state," he said.
Shuhaily, 54, pleaded not guilty to two charges of
voluntarily causing hurt
to two Special Branch policemen last month.
Shuhaily, charged as a summoned person, was accused of causing hurt to Lance Corporals Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Driman, 25, and Mohamad Faiz Saman, 40, at Counter J on the fifth floor of KLIA Terminal 1 between 1.27pm and 1.35pm on Sept 28.
The charges carries a maximum jail term of a year, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
Shuhaily was released after a family friend posted bail of RM1,500 with one surety for each charge.
He will return to the court on Nov 25 for case management.
Earlier, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said Shuhaily's
service status
has been referred to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) for legal advice.
He said Shuhaily's assignment at MCBA was based on a two-year secondment contract from the police, which had received the King's consent.
He said suspension from duty will depend on the A-GC's advice and contract termination must be submitted to the King.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PHB acquires RM300mil logistics property in Penang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) has acquired a logistics property in Bayan Lepas Waterfront, Penang, from Titijaya Land Bhd for RM300 million as part of its strategy to expand its logistics portfolio and strengthen recurring income streams.
The logistics commercial complex is fully leased to DHL Properties (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd, providing PHB with a stable rental income stream.
With this acquisition, PHB said the logistics segment now accounts for about 11 per cent of its total investment property portfolio, reflecting the company's growing focus on logistics and industrial assets.
The property was acquired from Aman Duta Sdn Bhd, an indirect subsidiary of Titijaya.
The asset comprises about 28,562.8 square metres of leasehold land in the Barat Daya district, together with a purpose-built, three-storey logistics commercial complex.
PHB Group managing director Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad said the acquisition would strengthen the company's presence in one of Malaysia's key logistics hubs while supporting its portfolio diversification strategy.
"The complex's location in Bayan Lepas Waterfront positions us to benefit from continued growth across Penang's logistics sector.
"Importantly, this asset provides long-term income visibility through a quality tenant and a stable lease structure. This is in line with our strategy to enhance our portfolio yield and strengthen our recurring income streams.
"As demand for quality logistics space continues to rise, this acquisition is an opportunity to enhance our portfolio's performance and deliver competitive returns for Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) unit holders," he said.
Titijaya Land group managing director Datuk Lim Poh Yit said the transaction reflected the company's commitment to creating value through quality income-generating real estate investments and strategic asset management.
"This transaction demonstrates our proactive approach to managing our property portfolio and unlocking asset value. We remain focused on our core property development business and on pursuing opportunities that support the group's long-term growth and create sustainable value for our stakeholders," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-Axis Incorporation adviser loses appeal over false financial statements
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Kuala Lumpur High Court has dismissed an appeal by Lee Koon Huat, a former adviser to Axis Incorporation Bhd's board of directors, and upheld his conviction and sentence for offences involving the submission of false financial statements to Bursa Malaysia.
High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin ruled that the prosecution had proven the charges against Lee beyond reasonable doubt.
In a statement, the Securities Commission (SC) said the High Court found that the conviction was sound and there were no grounds to interfere with the Sessions Court's decision.
The High Court also agreed with the SC's submission that the sentence was appropriate given Lee's role in the offences.
It subsequently upheld the Sessions Court's sentence of six months' imprisonment and a fine of RM200,000 for each charge.
Following the ruling, Lee applied for a stay of execution of the prison sentence and fine.
Lee was initially charged at the Sessions Court on March 26, 2013, with four counts under Section 122C(c), read together with Section 122B(a)(bb), of the Securities Industry Act 1983.
The charges involved abetting Axis in submitting false financial statements relating to its revenue for the financial year 2007.
According to the SC, evidence presented during the trial established that Lee had instructed the inflation of Axis' reported revenue in its four unaudited quarterly results for that financial year.
The SC had also previously charged three former Axis executive directors, Lee Han Boon, Saipuddin Lim Abdullah and Koh Tee Jin, with five counts each of knowingly permitting the submission of false financial statements relating to the company's revenue for the financial years 2007 and 2008.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysians missing in Nepal: Families facing 6-9 months' wait for death certification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Families of the 54 Malaysians missing in Nepal would need to wait at least six to nine months for letters of presumed death, despite Nepal cutting the waiting period from 12 years to 45 days.
Malaysia Solidarity Families in Hope (MASFIH)'s spokesman Dr R. Manivannan said the letters were needed for families to obtain death certificates and access their missing relatives' assets to settle outstanding liabilities.
"It will take at least six to nine months or at the best case scenario, and that is why we are concerned," he told reporters after meeting with Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan today.
Under Nepali law, a person had to be missing for 12 years before being legally declared dead, but on Oct 9, President Ram Chandra Paudel shortened the period to 45 days for victims of the recent landslide and flooding.
This is as thousands remain unaccounted for after the disaster.
Manivannan said Nepal had initially said the ordinance only needed cabinet approval, but now it must also be passed by its Parliament and gazetted.
He said Nepal was also holding a public inquiry into objections concerning its own missing citizens, which he expected would cover foreigners.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan had earlier said Malaysia was
awaiting details
of Nepal's special order and would monitor developments closely.
In Malaysia, meanwhile, Manivannan said it was unclear whether the National Registration Department (NRD) would recognise Nepal's letter to issue death certificates, as this was the first such case.
He said it was also uncertain whether the 54 cases would be processed collectively or individually, a step that could take another one to two months.
He said that even with death certificates, families could only access funds such as Employees Provident Fund (EPF) savings via a nominee, while other assets would require probate or letters of administration from the courts.
"So only after that, the families will be able to access the funds and the assets," he said.
Manivannan said MASFIH had submitted 52 questions on these issues to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) through the Foreign Ministry a week ago, but had yet to receive a response.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man dies after being trapped in paper mill machine in Bentong
Article:
KUANTAN: A man died after apparently becoming trapped in a machine while carrying out maintenance work at a paper mill in the Bentong Industrial Park, Karak.
Bentong acting district police chief DSP Azmi Mahmod said police received a call through the MERS 999 emergency system at 11.56pm, following which a team from the Bentong District Criminal Investigation Division and Karak Police Station was dispatched to the scene.
He said an inspection found that the victim, Muhammad Saifulnizam Miskam, 32, a worker at the mill, was trapped inside a machine and had lost consciousness.
"Preliminary investigations found no criminal element. The victim's body was sent to the Forensic Unit of Bentong Hospital for further action," he said in a statement today.
Azmi said the case had been classified as sudden death, while further investigations were ongoing to determine the cause and exact circumstances of the incident.
He also advised the public against any speculation and to allow the authorities to conduct their investigations.
The statement also said that all personnel at the Bentong District Police Headquarters extended their condolences to the victim's family.

Title: Toddlers tied up with rags: 11 daycare workers jailed in Indonesia
Article:
YOGYAKARTA: An Indonesian court sentenced 11 childcare workers on Wednesday to up to three years in prison for abusing toddlers at a daycare centre in a case that sparked nationwide outrage.
Police had arrested the workers, all women, in April along with the principal of the facility and the head of the foundation that ran it.
The arrests came after CCTV footage circulating on social media showed children, most under the age of two, lying on the floor wearing only nappies, their hands and feet bound with rags.
Some of the children's mothers wiped away tears as Judge Sunaryanto handed down each sentence, ranging from two to three years, at a court in Yogyakarta on Java island.
The workers were "lawfully and convincingly proven to have committed the criminal offence of participating in placing a child in a situation of abuse and neglect, as well as participating in acts of violence against a child, carried out on an ongoing basis," said the judge who, like many Indonesians, has one name.
Imedia Dwi Anjani, whose four-year-old son was a pupil at the daycare, wept as she told AFP afterwards: "These children need a lot of therapy, so if the perpetrators are only sentenced to 2 years or 2.6 years, in our view as parents, that's not fair."
The footage of conditions at the facility triggered a public scandal, and the centre was closed soon afterwards.
Police later said they had found 20 children crammed into a room just three metres  long by three metres wide.
They estimated that more than half of the about 100 children at the daycare were maltreated.
City police chief Eva Guna Pandia said at the time that the women had told police they tied up some of the children to prevent them from disturbing others.
They also said the centre was understaffed, with not enough personnel to bathe and dress the children.
Parent Noorman Windarto told AFP in April his son was tied up and repeatedly hospitalised with pneumonia during his time at the centre, while his daughter sometimes came home with bruises her handlers said she must have sustained elsewhere.
The principal and foundation head will be judged at a later date.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'Eat the rich': Thousands protest graft, wildfires in Indonesia
Article:
JAKARTA: Thousands of Indonesians protested in Jakarta and other cities Wednesday against economic hardship, graft and the government's handling of devastating wildfires emitting a toxic haze that has sickened thousands.
Many demonstrators held up the three-finger salute of rebellion from dystopian franchise "The Hunger Games" and waved posters with angry messages such as: "Hungry? Eat the Rich!" and "If we burn, you burn with us."
Many placards expressed anger towards President Prabowo Subianto, whose popularity two years into his term has reached record lows amid claims of widespread government corruption and growing authoritarianism.
"Hey Wok! Nobody paid us. We all hate you for free," stated one sign, using a pejorative for the president, while another blared: "No Clean Air Under Dirty Government."
Protester Sekar, 37, told AFP her "heart is shattered" by the plight of compatriots battling months of wildfires and haze while also contending with the effects of a weakening currency and higher prices.
"I came here from home with the intention of protecting the students" who called the demonstration, Sekar told AFP.
"I will be looking for any police officers who lay hands on them and take them away, and I will be the first to step forward to defend them."
Police said about 14,000 of its officers, as well as soldiers, had deployed to keep a lid on the demonstrations in Jakarta.
AFP witnessed some pushing and shoving between front-row protesters and officers trying to keep the surging crowd away from Jakarta's central Bundaran HI public square, surrounded by businesses and embassies.
Some in the crowd hurled half-empty plastic water bottles at law enforcers.
- 'THEY CANNOT BREATHE' -
The protest organising committee, which calls itself SADAR, meaning "aware" in Bahasa Indonesia, said the action was meant to mark a "revolution that is being proclaimed."
The group is demanding that the government declare a national emergency to unlock more resources to fight wildfires across the vast archipelago.
Deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas says the blazes have destroyed more than 1.9 million hectares in the nine months to September.
"Hundreds and thousands of people are suffering" from the fires, said protester Annette Mau, 47, of the Indonesian Mothers' Alliance, an NGO.
"Tens of thousands of babies are suffering from health problems. They cannot breathe" because of the fires emitting a toxic haze that has spread far across the region.
The pollution has also damaged Indonesia's relations with its neighbours.
Singapore's Foreign Minister Vivian Balakrishnan was expected to meet Prabowo in Jakarta on Wednesday, a day after saying the haze was "not a natural phenomenon" and the fires "were caused by human action."
Annette accused the government of "trying to cover" up the problem rather than address it.
"They're trying to make excuses," she said.
"We are being oppressed by the tyrannical regime."
A statement sent to AFP by protest organisers said that under Prabowo, "the sovereignty of the ruling class takes precedence over the sovereignty of the people."
They pointed to "mismanagement of the debt-burdened economy; environmental and energy exploitation that has triggered an ecological crisis; and the erosion of the rule of law and democracy."
There were also protests in the cities of Bandung outside Jakarta, Malang and Yogyakarta elsewhere on Java island, and Makassar on the south of Sulawesi island.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Foreign e-commerce platforms to face e-invoicing, must open local offices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Finance Ministry will impose e-invoicing on foreign e-commerce platforms and their vendors, which will have to open offices in Malaysia.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Seri Armizan Mohd Ali said the Finance Ministry would implement the measure soon as an immediate step to monitor foreign platforms.
"The Finance Ministry will also soon impose e-invoicing on these foreign platforms and their related vendors.
"With e-invoicing, they will be required to open offices in the country so that we can monitor them.
"That is the immediate action that will be carried out through the Finance Ministry," he said when winding up the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat.
Meanwhile, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman (Muda-Muar) also asked whether the Competition Commission (MyCC) would investigate possible collusion in the fee increases, saying TikTok Shop raised its fees each time after Shopee did.
Armizan said MyCC had completed a market review on the digital economy, which was recently presented to the National Digital Economy and Fourth Industrial Revolution Council.
"The prime minister received the document and directed MyCC to look into the issue thoroughly," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sinkhole appears in Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A 2.5m-wide, 4m-deep sinkhole opened on Lebuhraya Mayang Pasir this afternoon, forcing a road closure and emergency repair works.
State Infrastructure Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said initial checks indicated that a dislocated joint in a sewer pipe could have caused the incident.
Zairil said based on a report by the Public Works Department (PWD), the sinkhole was detected about 2pm near an open field at Lorong Mayang Pasir 4.
"The affected stretch has been closed to traffic, with motorists advised to use Lebuh Mayang Pasir, Jalan Mahsuri and Lorong Mayang Pasir 1 as alternative routes.
An emergency response team has been mobilised to the site to secure the area, divert sewage flow and carry out rectification works, he added.
Zairil said the repair works are targeted for completion by Nov 7, subject to weather conditions.
The affected area has been cordoned off with plastic barriers, while monitoring was being carried out to ensure public safety.
Earlier, Pantai Jerejak assemblyman Fahmi Zainol urged nearby residents to exercise caution when travelling through the area as investigations were under way.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: TikTok accounts for 81pc of 47,412 cyberbullying posts flagged by MCMC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: TikTok accounted for 81 per cent of the 47,412 cyberbullying-related posts identified by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for removal from January to yesterday.
Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Facebook accounted for the second-largest share, at 12 per cent, Bernama reported.
"The cyberbullying content identified by MCMC since the beginning of the year was based on public complaints," he told reporters as quoted by the news agency.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said MCMC was examining the misuse of messaging applications such as WhatsApp and Telegram, particularly their end-to-end encryption features, which allow private groups to operate beyond public view.
He expressed concern that cyberbullying could originate or spread within such groups, making them an area requiring closer scrutiny.
"I am concerned that certain communication platforms, such as WhatsApp and Telegram, use end-to-end encryption, allowing groups to be created without public knowledge.
"These are private rather than public groups, and bullying sometimes begins or becomes widespread within them. This is among the issues MCMC is examining," he said.
Fahmi said the review also covered the misuse of messaging platforms to sell prohibited goods, including drugs.
He said the matter needed to be examined in relation to the Online Safety Act although private messaging services were not currently covered by the legislation.
"The review of private communication platforms is ongoing, and no measures have been implemented at this stage. Although these platforms fall outside the Act, we will continue examining their impact," he said.
Fahmi added that concerns raised during discussions with police, alongside public complaints about the harmful effects of these platforms, underscored the need for closer scrutiny.

Title: Anwar decries tendency to label others 'murtad', 'munafik'
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has criticised certain people for readily labelling others as
murtad
(apostates) and
munafik
(hypocrites) despite having only limited religious knowledge.
The prime minister said the tendency to judge others based solely on limited religious knowledge reflected a deeper problem, namely a failure to develop a sound understanding of Islam and put its values into practice in daily life.
He said the tradition of scholarship and enlightenment must be strengthened to ensure that religious discussions do not spark tensions, but instead foster greater understanding among the public.
"Nowadays, there are many problems arising from people who study a little religion and immediately pass judgment, becoming
takfiri
by declaring others apostates and labelling them hypocrites.
"When matters are debated in Parliament, they call the leaders hypocrites and even label their budgets as hypocritical," he said during the Majlis Ilmu Madani Bersama Perdana Menteri programme attended by prominent Indonesian preacher Abdul Somad Batubara.
Present were Anwar's wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail; Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
Anwar did not name the people he was talking about, but recently, Pas secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan had used the word
munafik
while debating the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat.
Takiyuddin was told to withdraw the use of the word, but
refused to do so
.
Anwar said leaders have a responsibility to set good examples, particularly in upholding a tradition of scholarship, moderation and tolerance.
"When formulating the budget previously, we asked what could be done to benefit Islam and what more could be added.
"In the past, we neglected madrasahs, pondok schools and pesantren (traditional Islamic boarding schools), but we have rebuilt them. We also sidelined sheikhs and religious teachers, but now we invite them and seek their views," he said.
He said an approach based on wisdom, good counsel and constructive debate was essential in the context of Malaysia's multi-religious society.
"Why have we revived these Madani lectures, study sessions and talks? It is because any change must come from reason, but it must also be guided by examples from the Islamic system of governance, which teaches that responsibility rests with everyone," he said.
Anwar said efforts to uplift the standing of the Muslim community must begin with the pursuit of knowledge and greater awareness, alongside the cultivation of good morals and character.
He said a lack of understanding should not be addressed merely by highlighting problems, but must instead be followed by efforts to find solutions through knowledge.
"I just want to point out that this is symptomatic of the real problem, including among those who profess Islam, yet fail to set a good example in terms of morals, character, moderation and tolerance."

Title: Maxis neither denies nor confirms merger report
Article:

Title: CTOS still assessing impact of cybersecurity incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd is continuing to assess the operational and financial implications of its previously disclosed cybersecurity incident as it strengthens measures to protect personal and customer data.
In its latest quarterly results announcement, the credit reporting group said it was enhancing its cybersecurity, data governance and information security measures amid tighter regulatory scrutiny.
"Following the cybersecurity incident disclosed under material events during and subsequent to the financial period, the group will continue to assess related operational and financial implications," it said.
It added that measures were being implemented to strengthen its operations and restore stakeholder confidence.
CTOS' net profit rose 11.5 per cent to RM27.54 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM24.69 million a year earlier, as revenue increased 5.5 per cent to RM87.56 million year-on-year.
For the first nine months, net profit increased 14 per cent to RM68.71 million from RM60.29 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 7.5 per cent to RM256.02 million from RM238.08 million.
However, CTOS said segment profit from its Malaysian operations remained flat year-on-year during the nine-month period, despite higher revenue across all customer segments.
It attributed the performance to higher operating expenses for cloud migration and infrastructure modernisation, as well as the suspension of certain credit reporting services.
The company did not quantify the financial impact of the cybersecurity incident in the information provided.
CTOS said it would continue investing selectively in artificial intelligence, digital products, alternative data, analytics and technology infrastructure to strengthen its capabilities, improve operating efficiency and support sustainable revenue growth.

Title: CTOS Q3 net profit rises 11.5pct to RM27.54mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: CTOS Digital Bhd's net profit rose 11.5 per cent to RM27.54 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026, from RM24.69 million a year earlier, supported by higher revenue.
Revenue for the quarter increased 5.5 per cent to RM87.56 million from RM83.01 million in the corresponding period, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia.
CTOS declared a third interim single-tier dividend of 0.70 sen per share for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026, payable on Jan 27, 2027.
The credit reporting group said its Malaysian operations recorded a 33 per cent increase in segment profit to RM24.5 million from RM18.4 million in the preceding quarter, driven by higher revenue and a gain from the disposal of an investment in an associate.
However, segment profit from international operations, comprising its alternative data credit-scoring businesses in Indonesia and the Philippines, fell 62.8 per cent to RM1.3 million from RM3.4 million in the preceding quarter.
The decline was mainly due to non-recurring expenses, including withholding tax on dividends and retrospective staff cost adjustments.
International revenue slipped 1.7 per cent to RM13.9 million from RM14.1 million, reflecting slower sales growth.
For the first nine months of 2026, CTOS' net profit increased 14 per cent to RM68.71 million from RM60.29 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 7.5 per cent to RM256.02 million from RM238.08 million, supported by growth in its Malaysian and international operations.

Title: PG Doraisamy emerges as substantial shareholder in Kumpulan Jetson
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PG Doraisamy P Gopal, who was involved in an earlier attempt to overhaul Kumpulan Jetson Bhd's board of directors, has emerged as a substantial shareholder of the company with a 5.13 per cent direct stake.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia today, Kumpulan Jetson said Doraisamy held 23.53 million shares following the acquisition of 553,700 shares through an open-market transaction on Oct 26.
The shares are registered under CGS International Nominees Malaysia (Tempatan) Sdn Bhd in a pledged securities account belonging to Doraisamy.
Doraisamy was among five shareholders who sought to remove Jetson's then-board of directors and appoint a new one in April 2025.
The group also included Yudishthiran Doraisamy, Dhayalini PG Doraisamy, Wong Hong Yuk and Teoh Cheng Fang.
The move eventually led to the appointment of five directors nominated by the shareholder group in September that year.
According to MyBursa, Yudishthiran and Dhayalini currently hold 3.68 per cent and 3.65 per cent of Jetson respectively.
Together with Doraisamy's 5.13 per cent interest, the three individuals hold a combined 12.46 per cent stake in the company.
Kumpulan Jetson's largest shareholder is executive deputy chairman Datuk Seri Baljinder Singh, who holds 13.45 per cent.
The company is involved in manufacturing, construction and property development, as well as hostel management.

Title: [UPDATED] Malaysia opts for diplomacy to address Myanmar refugee issue
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: Malaysia has opted for a diplomatic approach with Myanmar to address the issue of refugees from the country living in Malaysia, despite international criticism of the government's handling of the crisis, said Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The Prime Minister said the approach was aimed at finding a solution after decades of criticism and condemnation against Myanmar, spanning 20 to 30 years, had failed to bring about significant changes to its policies.
He said Malaysia's efforts to establish diplomatic ties with Myanmar did not mean it agreed with or endorsed the country's treatment of the Rohingya ethnic minority, but rather served as a channel to secure cooperation in addressing the refugee issue.
"So, I think the way forward is to try to establish diplomatic relations with Myanmar.
"We are not saying that we agree with the expulsion of these people (refugees). We are not saying that we condone what has been done, but I have said that we want to be friends with Myanmar," he said.
He was responding to a question on Myanmar refugees during a question-and-answer session at the Majlis Ilmu Madani Bersama Perdana Menteri, attended by prominent Indonesian preacher Ustaz Abdul Somad Batubara, here today.
Anwar said discussions with Myanmar had resulted in an agreement for the country to repatriate some of its citizens in Malaysia at its own expense, including using its military aircraft and vessels.
He said about 10,300 Myanmar refugees had been repatriated so far, with another 3,000 expected to undergo the repatriation process this month.
He said the initiative was a temporary measure Malaysia could implement to address the refugee issue, although he acknowledged that it was insufficient to resolve the problem entirely.
"Is it enough? No. Does this mean I condone all its transgressions? No. But I think this is a temporary measure we can take," he said.
However, Anwar stressed that security must be prioritised during the repatriation process, given concerns that those returning to Myanmar could face risks to their personal safety.
He said Malaysia had sought security assurances from the Myanmar authorities but acknowledged that its ability to influence the situation in the country was limited.
The Prime Minister said Malaysia would therefore continue to use diplomatic channels to secure Myanmar's cooperation, including to gradually reduce the number of refugees in the country.

Title: At least 30 killed as two high-speed trains collide in Spain
Article:
MADRID: At least 30 people were killed when two high-speed trains collided in Spain on Wednesday, the second deadly accident in less than a year on the line connecting Madrid to the southern Andalusia region, regional authorities said.
Footage from regional Castilla-La Mancha Television showed a derailed train with at least one carriage remaining on an elevated section of track while twisted metal, broken panels and wreckage could be seen strewn across an embankment beneath the line.
Miguel, a passenger travelling with several colleagues in the rear car of one of the trains, described to COPE radio the moment of the accident.
"We heard a massive roar, a truly enormous thud that went on for 10 seconds, as if the train were about to derail. Through the right-hand window, we could see a wrecked train – I imagine it must have been the other one," he said.
Castilla-la Mancha regional government said the death toll had risen to 30 from 10 after earlier warning it could rise.
The collision comes nine months after an accident between high-speed trains belonging to the same operators on the same line that killed 46 people.
That crash in January, which occurred after a train derailed and smashed into an oncoming train near Adamuz, in Cordoba province, triggered a debate about the level of investment in railway maintenance in recent years.--REUTERS

Title: Father's lessons in resilience paved way for Nurhidayah's success [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A resilient spirit instilled in her from childhood helped Superintendent Nurhidayah Damanhoori prove that women can lead the police mounted unit, a role demanding physical endurance, specialised skills and discipline.
She made history in 2018 as the first woman appointed commanding officer of the unit since its establishment in 1984.
For Nurhidayah, who is the Internal Security and Public Order Department assistant director of development, technical and finance, the achievement came through life experiences, the courage to embrace new challenges and a willingness to learn.
She said her late father, Damanhoori Salikin, played a pivotal role in shaping her physical and mental resilience from an early age.
Although she was born and raised in Johor Baru, she grew up in a rural lifestyle, frequently accompanying her father on outdoor activities.
"I come from a family that lived modestly. My father trained me extensively, helping me grow into a woman who was physically resilient and mentally strong.
"From a young age, I had already learned how to grow crops in a garden, raise livestock and spend days at sea gathering its bounty.
"To put it simply, my late father raised me as he would a son. Most of my childhood playmates were also boys. I only played war games and had no interest in games traditionally associated with girls," she said.
The upbringing laid the foundation for her decision to join the uniformed services after graduating from Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia.
Her father, who understood her personality, encouraged her to apply to become either a police inspector or a captain in the armed forces.
She began training as a police inspector cadet on July 15, 2007, at the Police Training Centre, here.
She was subsequently assigned to the Criminal Investigation Department as an investigating officer at the age of 24.
"Investigating murder, rape and infant death cases, as well as handling bodies and attending court proceedings, helped shape my character.
"I also served as a senior investigating officer in the Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department  where I witnessed firsthand the impact of road accidents on victims who had left home to earn a living but never returned.
"Looking back, these experiences had an enormous impact on shaping my identity and character today," she said.
Her interest in animals and physically demanding activities eventually led her to equestrian sports. In 2015, she began learning to ride at the Universiti Teknologi Malaysia Equestrian Sports Club in Skudai.
In September 2016, while attending a riding class there, she encountered the police mounted unit personnel on duty and took the initiative to ask about joining the unit.
Her determination paid off when she received a transfer order to serve as head of the unit in Putrajaya.
She is also among a small group of female police officers to hold four specialised qualifications: the horseman proficiency badge, the diving proficiency badge, the parachuting proficiency badge and the force's full Class B motorcycle licence, which permits the riding of high-powered motorcycles.
These achievements reflect her involvement in disciplines requiring courage, physical endurance and specialised skills, alongside her leadership responsibilities.
Nurhidayah acknowledged that the appointment initially felt daunting.
However, she said the greatest challenge was not physical endurance but mastering horse handling and leading personnel with far more experience than she had.
"Some members of the unit have decades of experience handling horses. I therefore chose to respect their expertise and was never too proud to learn from those under my command," she said.
She also demonstrated her ability in equestrian endurance riding, becoming the first commanding officer to qualify for a 120km event after competing in events over 40km, 80km and 100km.
However, she said her most difficult experience as commanding officer was not dealing with aggressive horses but making the decision to end the suffering of an animal with severe injuries.
She recalled an incident in which one of the unit's horses broke its leg in an accident while on duty.
A veterinarian recommended euthanasia because the horse could not be saved, leaving her with an emotionally difficult decision.
Yet she also remembers successfully treating another horse that had previously been recommended for euthanasia.
She tried a homemade medicinal remedy and the horse recovered and remains alive today.
Nurhidayah also faced tense situations while the mounted unit was patrolling the national border alongside the General Operations Force, including an incident involving gunfire from a neighbouring country.
She said the proficiency of the officers and their horses enabled them to bring the situation under control without further incident.
Despite the demands of her career, Nurhidayah said the greatest sacrifice for female police officers, particularly mothers, was time with their families.
The need to remain on standby for duty at any time often affects the time officers can spend with their children.
When her daughter was an infant, Nurhidayah sometimes had to bring her to the office to stay overnight because of her 24-hour duty commitments.
"My child has already learned to say, 'a police officer's child must be strong.' When my daughter was still a baby and I had not even completed my confinement period, she would often accompany me to spend the night at the office while I was on 24-hour duty.
"My family's support gives me the strength to continue serving. I also draw on the upbringing given to me by my mother, Hanim Sheikh Yousoff, who has always reminded me never to abuse my rank or mistreat junior officers," she said.
Nurhidayah encourages more young women to join the force, provided they are prepared for the challenges and sacrifices of a career in the uniformed services.
"There is nothing to fear if your spirit is ready to make sacrifices for our beloved country. However, we must remain realistic: every career in the world comes with its own challenges," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Netanyahu survives election setback as Israeli Jews deliver clear backing
Article:
JERUSALEM: Benjamin Netanyahu won the support of an unexpectedly clear majority of Israeli Jews in an election billed as a major turning point in his nation's history, apparently ensuring he will survive as prime minister at least in a caretaker role.
With around 70.7 per cent of votes tallied on Wednesday morning, Israeli media forecast Netanyahu's bloc of right-wing, far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties winning 54 seats in parliament, far surpassing 47 for the opposition bloc of rival Gadi Eisenkot. Parties representing Israelis of Arab descent would win 19.
The results could still change as counting continued, but a victory for Eisenkot appeared increasingly out of reach, as his bloc of anti-Netanyahu parties from centre-left to hard-right underperformed pre-election polls that forecast a tight race.
While Netanyahu lost his bloc's majority in the 120-seat Knesset, as expected, opponents were left with no hope of unseating him without some form of backing of Arab parties, which many have ruled out. Even then, he would remain as caretaker during any coalition negotiations, or until a new election next year.
SECURITY FIGHT SHARPENS
Netanyahu, addressing his Likud party's faithful after 3am at the party's election headquarters in Jerusalem, called for the formation of "a strong, right-wing national government."
He also highlighted Israel's military successes and raised the prospect of renewed joint military action against Iran alongside his ally, US President Donald Trump.
"Israel faces a singular historical opportunity, together with our partner President Trump, to remove the existential threat of Iran once and for all. But ulterior motives must not divert us from this sacred mission," he said.
Trump, who had called on Israeli voters to keep Netanyahu in power so they could "finish the job" in Iran, said Netanyahu had done "very well" thanks to his own endorsement.
"I think when the endorsement went out, it helped him a lot, but I actually heard he did pretty well. It might be winning or tie. The tie is sort of considered a win in that case because it's a big chess match," Trump said early on Wednesday at a campaign stop in Texas.
EISENKOT CALLS ON SECURITY CHIEFS TO RESIST PRESSURE
Eisenkot acknowledged that Netanyahu was still in office as a caretaker, but said the prime minister had lost public support and urged him to retire from politics. He also issued a warning that Netanyahu might use security for political ends.
"I call on the heads of the security establishment and the civil service: Netanyahu is a caretaker prime minister, without a mandate or the people's trust," he said.
"Remember that you serve only the state and the interests of Israel's citizens. Stand firm in the face of any attempt to challenge you. You have my unequivocal backing. Netanyahu, do not dare use Israel's security for your political needs."
The election was the first held in Israel since Hamas-led fighters killed 1,200 people and carried off 251 hostages in attacks that shattered the country's sense of security and plunged it into war in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran.
The war in Gaza, which flattened the territory and killed 74,000 Palestinians, has left Israel increasingly isolated on the world stage, with a decisive shift in global public opinion against it, including in its closest ally the United States.
Netanyahu himself is wanted by the International Criminal Court in The Hague on war crimes charges he calls absurd, and faces corruption charges in Israel that he dismisses as an establishment plot.
DECISIVE SHIFT IN ISRAELI POLITICS
His continued support from most Israeli Jews was a clear sign of the decisive shift in Israeli politics that he has presided over as the dominant political figure of the era.
His brand of unapologetic Jewish nationalism, support for settlement on occupied Palestinian land and contempt for all foreign criticism is now firmly entrenched as the Israeli mainstream.
The centre-left that dominated Israel for the first half of its history and had led negotiations to exchange land for peace with Arab neighbours has been reduced to a small fringe.
Nearly all Jewish parties now share Netanyahu's rejection of any eventual independent state for Palestinians, the basis of internationally endorsed peace talks since the 1990s, when he first came to power as Israel's youngest-ever leader.
After a spell in the wilderness as a right-wing maverick, he returned to power in 2009 and has remained ever since, apart from a period of 18 months when a rickety coalition of opponents managed to lever him out after four inconclusive elections in two years.
Both sides saw Tuesday's election as a decisive turning point for the nation, driving turnout to 77.7 per cent, the highest in more than two decades and around 7 percentage points higher than in 2022.
Turnout was particularly high among Israelis of Palestinian descent, who make up more than a fifth of the population but whose representatives have historically been excluded from the cabinet. Many were motivated by what they see as open racism from Netanyahu's cabinet, which includes a party leader convicted of inciting racial hatred against Arabs.
The headquarters of the Joint List, an alliance of several Arab parties, burst into whistles and applause when exit polls were released.
"We refuse the occupation and racism, and we will remain here," said Faten Gattas, a candidate in the Joint List, in a speech at the alliance's headquarters in Nazareth.--REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Appeal court imposes 20-year sentence on headmaster for child sex offences
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — The Court of Appeal today sentenced a headmaster to 20 years in jail and 11 strokes of the cane for making pornography and committing physical sexual assault against a standard six student five years ago.
A three-judge panel, chaired by Justice Datuk Noorin Badaruddin alongside Justices Datuk Mohd Radzi Abdul Hamid and Datuk Meor Hashimi Abdul Hamid, dismissed Anuar Kintan’s appeal against his conviction and sentence of nine years and eight strokes of the cane imposed by the High Court for the charge of making pornography.
The panel, however, allowed the prosecution’s appeal to overturn the lower court’s decisions to acquit and discharge Anuar on the second charge of physical sexual assault against the victim, who was 12 years old at the time.
The court subsequently convicted him of the charge, sentencing him to 11 years with three strokes of the cane.
Justice Noorin, who delivered the unanimous decision, ordered the sentences to be served consecutively. She also issued a warrant of committal for Anuar, 59, to begin his sentence today. He had previously obtained a stay of execution of the sentence and was released on bail of RM14,000 with one surety pending disposal of his appeal.
The court, meanwhile, upheld the lower court’s decision to acquit and discharge Anuar on the third and fourth charges, which involved physical sexual assault on the girl and uttering words intended to be heard by the victim for sexual purposes.
Justice Noorin said the victim had given direct testimony identifying the accused as the person who took the photographs, and that her testimony had been considered by the Sessions Court judge who accepted it.
She said the existence of the photographs was not an isolated circumstance, but was supported by forensic examination that identified the images in Anuar’s Realme mobile phone.
On the second charge, Justice Noorin said the court disagreed that the alibi evidence presented by Anuar had raised reasonable doubt.
The defence had put forward an alibi in which Anuar’s wife testified that he was at home with her, and not at the school, when the incident occurred.
Justice Noorin said the testimony of the victim’s friend provided material support for the prosecution’s case regarding the accused’s presence at the school on April 3, 2021, and his movements with the victim. Therefore, the alibi evidence presented by the accused did not raise reasonable doubt.
On April 19, 2024, the Sessions Court found Anuar guilty of the first offence for making pornography by taking photos of the victim and sentenced him to three years in jail and two strokes of the cane.
The Sessions Court also sentenced him to an additional one year’s imprisonment and two strokes of the cane under Section 16 (1) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017. The section provides for punishment if an offender commits a sexual crime while holding a position of trust over a child. The sentences were to run consecutively.
The Sessions Court, however, acquitted him of the second, third and fourth charges.
The High Court on Aug 15 last year increased the prison sentence for the first charge to nine years’ imprisonment and eight strokes of the cane and upheld his acquittal for the other three charges.
The offences were committed at a school in Perak in the middle of March 2021 and on April 3, 2021.
At the proceedings today, Anuar was represented by lawyer Amir Khusyairi Mohamad Tanusi while Deputy Public Prosecutors Azlina Mahmod and P. Sarulatha appeared for the prosecution. — Bernama

Title: PM says Budget 2027 reinforces Islam, criticises ‘hypocrite’ accusation
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that Budget 2027 was formulated to continue promoting Islam, including through specific measures to strengthen pondok religious schools nationwide.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the government had sought the views of Islamic scholars and religious teachers in drawing up the budget to ensure that the development needs of Islam received due attention.
He therefore criticised certain quarters for labelling the leader behind the Madani Government’s Budget 2027 as a “hypocrite”.
“When formulating Budget 2027, we asked what more could be done for Islam and what else could be added. In the past, we neglected pondok institutions and pesantren (Islamic boarding schools), but now we are rebuilding them.
“In the past, we sidelined the syeikhs, religious teachers and tuan-tuan guru (respected religious scholars), but now we invite them and seek their views,” he said when speaking at the Majlis Ilmu MADANI programme at Kompleks Seri Perdana here today, which featured renowned Indonesian preacher Ustaz Dr Abdul Somad Batubara as a guest.
Also present were the Prime Minister’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail; Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan; and Weststar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim.
Anwar admitted that he was somewhat angered by the matter but said he remained patient, describing it as a systemic problem.
“When the matter was debated in Parliament, he called the leader a hypocrite and the budget hypocritical. If I were to ask Ustaz Abdul Somad, he would say, ‘Be patient, Pak.’ My heart was boiling, but I remained patient and did not respond.
“I just want to say that this is merely symptomatic of the real problem … those who profess Islam do not help or set a good example in terms of morals, personal conduct, moderation and tolerance,” he said.
Previously, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul had directed Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) to withdraw the word “hypocrite” that he had used during the debate.
The Prime Minister also expressed his appreciation to Abdul Somad for sharing his knowledge at the programme, adding that the preacher’s advice was always taken seriously in efforts to make Malaysia a better country.
“Ustaz Abdul Somad is now a prominent figure, but he is also controversial in some respects because he is bold in his criticism, which can sometimes be sharp.
“His criticism reaches all those in power, including in Malaysia. However, based on our experience in matters of governance and procedures, we welcome such criticism and try to make improvements,” he said.

Title: High Court dismisses ex-Axis adviser’s appeal, upholds jail term and RM800,000 fine
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The High Court here today dismissed the appeal by former Axis Incorporation Bhd board adviser Lee Koon Huat against his conviction and sentence on four charges of abetting the furnishing of false financial statements to Bursa Malaysia.
In a statement today, the Securities Commission (SC) said Judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin held that the prosecution had proven the charges against Lee beyond reasonable doubt at trial and there were no grounds to interfere with the Sessions Court’s decision.
“The High Court further agreed with the SC’s submission that the sentence imposed against Lee was appropriate in view of Lee’s role in the commission of the offences.
“As such, the court dismissed Lee’s appeal against sentence and upheld the sentence imposed by the Sessions Court, being six months’ imprisonment and a fine of RM200,000 for each charge or in default, six months’ imprisonment,” it said.
The statement said, the court allowed Lee’s application for stay of execution in respect of the sentence of imprisonment, but declined to grant a stay in respect of the fine.
“Lee will have to pay a total fine of RM800,000 by today, failing which he will be imprisoned in default of the payment,” said the statement.
The SC said Lee was initially charged at the Sessions Court on 23 March 2013 with four charges under Section 122C(c) read together with Section 122B(a)(bb) of the Securities Industry Act 1983 (SIA) for abetting Axis in the furnishing of false financial statements relating to the revenue of Axis for the financial year 2007.
“Evidence adduced during the trial established that Lee had instructed the inflation of Axis’ reported revenue in its four unaudited quarterly results for the financial year 2007,” it said.
The SC had also previously charged three former Axis executive directors, Lee Han Boon, Saipuddin Lim Abdullah and Koh Tee Jin, with offences relating to the furnishing of false financial statements for the 2007 and 2008 financial years.
All three pleaded guilty and were sentenced to imprisonment terms ranging from one day to 12 months, while Lee Han Boon and Koh were also sentenced to fine of RM200,000 respectively.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Shoba Venu Gobal and prosecuting officers Low Wen Zhen, Eunice Ong, and Amina Qistina Mohd Idris appeared for the SC while Lee was represented by counsel Jason Ng Kau and Caroline Lee. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Dialogue with Myanmar offers best hope for Rohingya solution
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia has opted for diplomacy in dealing with the refugee issue involving Myanmar, despite facing international criticism over the government’s approach to resolving the matter, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the approach was necessary to seek a solution after years of criticism and condemnation directed at Myanmar had failed to bring about any significant change in the country’s policies.
“When I invited Myanmar President (Min Aung Hlaing), what was the objective? In my two previous meetings with him, I urged him to moderate his stance. We have been expressing anger and criticising them for 20 or 30 years, but it has had no effect. There has been no change in policy.
“The people in Rakhine, the Rohingya, continue to suffer. Some 200,000 have fled here, placing a burden on us as well. The people, including the Malay community, are becoming increasingly upset over the situation
Anwar was speaking at the ‘Majlis Ilmu Madani’ programme at Kompleks Seri Perdana here today, featuring prominent Indonesian preacher Ustaz Dr Abdul Somad Batubara as a guest.
He was explaining Malaysia’s position on refugees from Myanmar, including the Rohingya, and efforts to facilitate their return to their country of origin. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Malaysia must embrace AI, quantum technology without losing cultural roots
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — Malaysia must continue to master emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI) and quantum computing, to remain competitive globally while preserving its religious and cultural identity, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said technological advancement was essential to ensuring the country kept pace with global developments, but must be anchored in religious faith, moral values, culture and literature.
“If we fail to master technology, others will overwhelm us. That is the principle. In the past, we fell behind because others mastered technology while we did not.
“But reaching for the sky must go hand in hand with being rooted in the ground. And what keeps us rooted? Our faith, morals, values, culture and literature,” he said.
He was speaking at the ‘Majlis Ilmu Madani’ programme at Kompleks Seri Perdana here today, featuring prominent Indonesian preacher Ustaz Dr Abdul Somad Batubara as a guest.
Also present were Anwar’s wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan, and Westar Group founder and managing director Tan Sri Dr Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim.
Anwar said the culture of seeking knowledge must be strengthened to address the tendency among some individuals to raise problems without offering solutions based on knowledge and rational thinking.
He said a lack of in-depth understanding across various fields, including religion, could lead to tensions when people pass judgment on issues without sufficient knowledge or careful consideration.
“Even today, some religious teachers create problems. They learn a little about religion and immediately pass judgment, becoming ‘takfiris’ who declare others apostates or accuse them of hypocrisy,” he said.
Takfir refers to the practice of one Muslim declaring another Muslim an infidel or apostate.
He said the government would continue to strengthen religious education institutions, including traditional religious learning and the study of turath, or the Islamic intellectual heritage.
Anwar said the government also organised the monthly Madani Scholars Forum for senior leadership, including Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, to encourage informed discussion on such issues.
“The forum is sponsored by a conglomerate, and we invite people to discuss these matters. We believe that without adequate preparation in knowledge and understanding, including in preaching, religious studies and jurisprudence, tensions will arise,” he said.
The Majlis Ilmu Madani programme, held at the Prime Minister’s official residence, is part of efforts to foster a society that values knowledge and appreciates the importance of proper conduct and good character.
Anwar conceived the programme after becoming Prime Minister in November 2022. It has since been expanded to venues nationwide. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin: More stringent checks at KLIA to combat drug smuggling
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — More stringent inspections are set to be implemented at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) following an increase in reported drug smuggling cases at the nation’s primary gateway, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He stated that the inspections will be highly rigorous with checking passengers from head-to-toe and will extend to all luggage or bags being carried.
“The current inspection practices are primarily focused on aviation security, such as the detection of firearms and sharp weapons.
“However, we will implement improvements to also curtail contraband and illegal items by strengthening 17 specific initiatives to be carried out by the home and transport ministries.
“We will also employ a profiling system, particularly for passenger arrivals from destinations we have identified as high-risk,” he said during a press conference at the Malaysia-Singapore RTS Link Security Joint Exercise closing ceremony held at the RTS Link Wadi Hana site here today.
Also present were Singapore’s Second Minister for Home Affairs Sim Ann and the Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure, and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh.
Saifuddin Nasution said the Home Ministry will also be identifying ‘blind spot’ areas that are not monitored by close circuit television (CCTV) cameras at the KLIA 1 and 2 terminals.
He said both KLIA 1 and 2 have 5,000 operational CCTV cameras, but said there are still ‘blind spot’ areas.
“The relevant department will be addressing this issue as part of the security enhancement process,” he said.
Separately, Saifuddin Nasution said the recent security exercise is essential for testing the level of preperation, response capabilities and coordination between agencies from Malaysia and Singapore.
He pointed out that such exercises are crucial for managing potential crises or emergencies once the service becomes operational.
“The RTS Link is expected to carry up to 10,000 passengers per hour in each direction, necessitating thorough preparation to ensure that any incidents can be handled effectively.
“This particular scenario presents a challenge that requires close coordination between the two countries – specifically in defining the responsibilities and actions of the relevant agencies in the event of a cross-border emergency,” he said.
Preparations for the exercise began in March under the coordination of the National Security Council (NSC) and involving 28 Malaysian ministries and agencies.

Title: Malaysia to deploy latest body scanners at RTS Link border checkpoint
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Latest technology scanners will be deployed at the Immigration, Customs and Quarantine (ICQ) Complex in Bukit Chagar here once the Johor Bahru–Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link starts operations early next year.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the implementation of this technology marks a first for Malaysia and serves as part of efforts to enhance security at the nation’s entry points.
He explained that the technology is capable of detecting objects carried on a person’s body, including items wrapped or concealed in specific materials intended to evade detection.
“A demonstration of this equipment was presented to me while I was reviewing security preparations for the Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Security Exercise (Field Training Exercise/FTX 2026).
“I was shown a system that is capable of detecting not just weapons, but anything else a person might be carrying on their body,’ he told reporters at the Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Security Exercise (FTX 2026) closing ceremony at the RTS Link Wadi Hana site here today.
Also present were Singapore’s Second Minister for Home Affairs Sim Ann an Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh.
Saifuddin Nasution said there is no longer any room or opportunity for anyone to evade detection if they attempt to conceal items as the equipment will identify them.
More than 100 of the latest scanning units will be deployed at the Bukit Chagar ICQ Complex.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail (left) presenting a memento to his Singapore counterpart Sim Ann, who is the Second Minister for Home Affairs, at the Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Security Exercise (FTX 2026) closing ceremony at the RTS Link Wadi Hana site Johor Bahru today, Oct 28, 2026. – Picture by Ben Tan
Saifuddin Nasution explained that these enhancements align with a Cabinet directive for the home and transport ministries to look into strengthening security at the nation’s entry points.
He added that both ministries, through their respective secretaries-generals, have proposed 17 initiatives, encompassing short to medium and long term measures.
“For the start, more targeted inspections will take place with a focus on passengers and goods arriving from locations identified as high-risk based on established profiles and past incidents.
“More intensive inspection protocols are being implemented to ensure that security at the country’s entry points remains resilient.
“There will also be improvements that extend to access passes management,” he said, adding that the passes had longer validity periods, but they will now be subject to annual renewal.

Title: Man remanded over Facebook caricature allegedly insulting police
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Oct 28 —  Police have arrested a 50-year-old local man in connection with an investigation into a caricature allegedly insulting the police that went viral on social media.
In a statement today, Kedah police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said the 50-year-old self-employed man was detained outside Menara Seri Wilayah P2a in Putrajaya yesterday.
He said police received a report on Oct 25 concerning a post uploaded by the owner of a Facebook account.
“The post depicted a caricature of two uniformed police officers wearing make-up and carrying women’s handbags at an airport, alongside the caption, ‘tak tau nak nangis ker or nak gelak’ (Not sure whether to cry or laugh),” the statement said.
Adzli said police had seized a mobile phone believed to have been used to make the post.
He said police were investigating the case under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code, Section 14 of the Minor Offences Act 1955 and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998, following 38 reports lodged in various states.
Adzli said the Langkawi Magistrate’s Court had granted a two-day remand order for the suspect, beginning today, to facilitate further investigations.
He advised the public to avoid making comments or speculating on the matter, as well as spreading unverified information that could disturb public order.
Adzli also warned that strict action would be taken against those who crossed the line, violated the law or attempted to provoke unrest that could compromise national security. — Bernama

Title: Ex-convicts among nine arrested in Miri grave desecration probe
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 28 — Police have arrested nine men believed to be involved in grave desecration activities in the Miri district during a special operation from October 11 to 17.
Sarawak acting police commissioner DCP Saifullizan Ishak said investigations revealed that three of the suspects had prior criminal records.
"Two of the three suspects were also believed to have been recently released from prison after serving sentences for the same offence and are believed to have recruited others to engage in grave desecration activities," he told a press conference at the Sarawak Police Contingent Headquarters (IPK) here today.
Saifullizan said further investigations and confessions from the suspects showed the activities had been carried out since Aug 6.
"Following our action and investigations, police have solved 15 reported grave desecration cases in the Miri district. Items seized to assist in the investigation include iron hammers, screwdrivers and various jewellery items such as rings, earrings, necklaces, bracelets, and old coins," he said.
He added that all arrested individuals are aged between 16 and 73, and police are investigating the case under Section 297 of the Penal Code for trespassing on burial places and related offences. — Bernama

Title: What if a fire breaks out on the RTS Link? Malaysia and Singapore put their rescue plans to the test
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — Malaysia and Singapore have demonstrated their ability to jointly manage cross-border emergencies involving the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, following a field exercise simulating a fire aboard a stranded train.
