Singapore’s Second Minister for Foreign Affairs and Second Minister for Home Affairs Sim Ann said the exercise, held yesterday, demonstrated effective coordination between agencies from both countries in responding swiftly and professionally to a simulated emergency.
She said three key outcomes stood out during the exercise, namely real-time communication, coordinated deployment of emergency personnel, and effective command and control.
“Malaysia’s operations centre at Bukit Chagar and Singapore’s ICA Integrated Operations Centre maintained real-time contact throughout the management of the incident.
“This enabled both countries to establish a joint situation picture and communicate their action plans to each other,” she said at the closing ceremony of the Malaysia-Singapore Cross-Border Joint Field Exercise for the RTS Link here today. Also present was Malaysia’s Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
Sim Ann said officers and station operators from both sides of the border also coordinated effectively in deploying personnel from fire and rescue, law enforcement and border control agencies.
She said the exercise further demonstrated that officers clearly understood their respective roles and responsibilities, even when managing a fast-moving crisis.
Highlighting the unique operational challenges of the RTS Link, Sim Ann said each train would carry more than 600 passengers, with services operating at short intervals and a peak capacity of up to 10,000 passengers per hour in each direction.
With each journey taking only five minutes, she said any disruption or emergency could affect a large number of passengers within a short period, requiring swift information sharing and close coordination between agencies operating under different legal and command structures.
“An emergency on board a crowded and fast-moving train leaves little room for error. By executing the response plans correctly and swiftly, we will be better prepared to save lives, minimise damage and restore normalcy quickly,” she said.
Sim Ann said operational agencies from both countries had been working together since 2023 to develop clear frameworks, laws and operational protocols to guide frontline responders in handling cross-border incidents once the RTS Link begins operations.
She said a tabletop exercise conducted last month had allowed agencies to test their emergency response plans involving natural hazards, medical emergencies, fires, and public order and security incidents before progressing to the field exercise.
“Readiness is proven only when those plans are put to the test,” she said, adding that the latest exercise provided valuable lessons for further improving joint response plans before an actual emergency occurs.
She stressed that the exercise was not an endpoint but an important milestone in ongoing preparations, with both countries expected to continue refining operational protocols and conducting regular joint exercises as the RTS Link moves towards operationalisation.
Sim Ann also described the RTS Link as more than a transport connection, saying it would bring the people, communities and economies of Malaysia and Singapore closer together by making daily cross-border travel faster and more convenient.
She expressed appreciation to the Malaysian government, the Johor state government and participating agencies for their close cooperation in organising the exercise, which she said reflected both countries’ shared commitment to ensuring safe and effective RTS Link operations. — Bernama

Title: Ex-Selangau MP Baru Bian fails to throw out PKR’s RM10m lawsuit over party exit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Ba’kelalan state assemblyman Baru Bian today failed in his bid to strike out a lawsuit filed by PKR seeking RM10 million in damages for allegedly breaching the terms of a bond after leaving the party following his victory in the 14th General Election (GE14) in 2018.
High Court judge Roslan Mat Nor dismissed the application by Baru, 68, to strike out the suit and challenge the jurisdiction of the High Court of Malaya to hear and decide PKR’s claim against him.
The court ordered the former Selangau Member of Parliament to pay RM4,000 in costs to PKR.
In his application, Baru said he signed the bond in Kuching on April 25, 2018, and that his involvement with PKR was confined to Sarawak.
“The plaintiff’s (PKR) action against me, even if proven, did not arise in Peninsular Malaysia. The claim arose in Sarawak,” he said in the application.
Baru is among 16 former Members of Parliament and state assemblymen sued by PKR secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh on behalf of the party for allegedly breaching the terms of a RM10 million bond they signed with the party.
Also named as defendants are Datuk Kamarudin Jaffar, Datuk Mansor Othman, Datuk Mohd Rashid Hasnon, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Abdullah and Datuk Seri R. Santhara Kumar.
Abdul Yunus Jamhari, Datuk Azman Nasrudin, Dr Afif Bahardin, Chong Fat Full, Daroyah Alwi, Haniza Mohamed Talha, Muhammad Hilman Idham, Muhammad Jailani Khamis, Robert Ling Kui Ee and Zulkifli Ibrahim were also named as defendants.
In separate suits filed on February 19 and 27, PKR claimed that under the operative clause of the bond, each defendant agreed to pay the party RM10 million within seven days after the occurrence of events such as resigning from the party, joining another political party or becoming an independent elected representative.
The plaintiff claimed that it had appointed each defendant as a candidate to contest in GE14 and that they subsequently won several parliamentary and state seats, leading to the formation of the federal government and several state governments.
“However, on February 24, 2020, each defendant ceased to be a party member after being elected under the party’s banner. They also expressed support for political coalitions other than PKR,” PKR said in its statement of claim.
PKR said that on March 11, 2020, the party decided to terminate the membership of each defendant with immediate effect, and a certificate dated March 16, 2020 was issued to confirm that their memberships had been terminated and to demand that each defendant pay the RM10 million bond, but they failed to do so. — Bernama

Title: GPS to contest all 82 seats in Sarawak election, says Abang Johari
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 28 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) will contest all 82 state seats in Sarawak’s 13th state election.
Sarawak Premier and GPS chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg said the decision was reached following a meeting with the presidents of the coalition’s component parties today.
“We do not yet know the election date as it will be determined by the Election Commission (EC). However, GPS is ready,” he told reporters after chairing the GPS Supreme Leadership Council meeting here.
Abang Johari said the coalition would await the EC’s announcement of the election dates before deciding its next course of action.
On seat allocations among GPS component parties, he said detailed discussions would be held based on the seats currently held by each party.
On October 23, Abang Johari announced the dissolution of the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly, effective October 26, to pave the way for the state election.
The EC is scheduled to hold a special meeting on November 6 to determine key election dates and discuss related matters.
In the 12th state election on December 18, 2021, GPS secured 76 of the 82 seats contested, while Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) won four and DAP two.
However, Sarawak’s political landscape changed following PSB’s dissolution in 2024, when three of its former assemblymen joined the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), a GPS component party, while another one opted to become an independent.
GPS comprises Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and PDP. — Bernama

Title: Motorcyclist killed in Klang after collision with 4WD sends him into trailer’s path
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 28 — A motorcyclist was killed after being run over by a trailer following a collision with a four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicle travelling in the emergency lane along Jalan Pintasan Pelabuhan Barat, Klang, near here at 9am today.
Klang Selatan police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said the 37-year-old local man was pronounced dead at the scene due to severe injuries. His body was taken to Tengku Ampuan Rahimah Hospital (HTAR) in Klang for a post-mortem.
“Preliminary investigations found that the victim is believed to have collided with the right side of the four-wheel-drive vehicle, which was travelling in the emergency lane. The impact caused him to fall into the right lane, where he was run over by a trailer travelling in the adjacent lane.
“The victim was riding alone from Klang towards the West Port. The drivers of the four-wheel-drive vehicle and the trailer were unhurt,” he said in a statement today.
Lim urged members of the public with information on the incident to assist in the investigation by contacting investigating officer Insp Mohamad Mustakin Najri at 012-5826983 or any nearby police station.
He also advised road users against using the emergency lane as a shortcut and urged them to remain vigilant, concentrate on driving and obey traffic rules to prevent similar incidents.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: All approved school projects will be completed, Fadhlina pledges
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The government has given its assurance that all approved school development projects will be implemented and completed, while projects that had to be cancelled due to specific factors will be resubmitted for fresh approval.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said issues such as land constraints and rising costs would not result in school development needs being neglected, adding that affected projects would be resubmitted to address the needs of the schools concerned.
“I wish to emphasise here that we will ensure every approved project is implemented and completed. I repeat, we will ensure that every approved project is implemented and completed,” she said when winding up the policy-level debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for the ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Fadhlina said the commitment covered schools nationwide, with the ministry continuing to prioritise safe, conducive and quality educational facilities, particularly in rural and remote areas.
She said 131 new school construction and replacement projects, costing more than RM14.789 billion in total, had been approved between 2023 and 2027.
Of these, nine were approved in 2023, 26 in 2024, 44 in 2025, 38 in 2026 and 14 in 2027.
Meanwhile, 292 projects to redevelop dilapidated school buildings in Sabah and Sarawak have been approved since 2023, involving RM10.29 billion, or 80 per cent of the total allocation channelled to the two states.
Fadhlina said the ministry was also leveraging Industrialised Building System (IBS) technology to accelerate school construction and classroom expansion, while reducing costs and construction waste.
Of the 777 additional classroom projects using IBS undertaken this year, 159 had been completed and handed over to the ministry. The remaining projects were being monitored to ensure completion by December, allowing the facilities to be used at the start of the next academic session.
She said the ministry had also introduced targeted school renovation and upgrading initiatives since 2024 to improve facilities more quickly without having to wait for large-scale development projects.
The initiative covered 50 schools in 2024, involving RM15 million; 309 schools in 2025, with an allocation of RM135 million; and 118 schools in 2026, with RM50 million allocated.
On bullying, Fadhlina said the 5,681 cases recorded from January to August this year reflected greater awareness and a growing willingness among victims, witnesses and school administrations to report incidents.
She said this would help prevent cases from being concealed to protect a school’s reputation.
“This shift in the reporting landscape has become particularly pronounced following the gazetting and enforcement of the Anti-Bullying Act 2026. We are now seeing investigations, comprehensive reporting and disciplinary action being carried out in accordance with existing regulations,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Klang art studio loses nearly RM2,000 in pre-dawn break-in, three nabbed
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 28 — An art studio owner lost nearly RM2,000 after the studio in Bandar Bukit Tinggi, Klang was believed to have been broken into by three men on October 24.
The South Klang district police chief ACP Lim Jit Huey said that in the incident around 4.20am, three suspects were believed to have prised open the grille door and wooden door of the premises before stealing the complainant’s belongings.
“Acting on information, the police arrested three men aged between 22 and 30 years on October 27. All the suspects have past criminal and drug records,” he said in a statement today.
Lim said all the suspects are now remanded for three days starting from today until October 31 to assist in the investigation.
He also requested the cooperation of the public who have information regarding the incident to contact investigating officer SJN Nurman Amri Abdul Rahman at 011-11559066, the South Klang IPD operations room at 03-33762222 or any nearby police station.
The case is being investigated under Section 457 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: Govt plans national drought response as El Niño threatens extreme heat in early 2027, Dewan Rakyat told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) will propose the development of a drought action plan to the National Disaster Management Council to strengthen preparedness for the phenomenon.
Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the proposal would be submitted for the council’s consideration, so that action plans for floods and droughts could also be developed, in addition to the existing National Haze Action Plan.
“This is something that will be brought to the National Disaster Management Council, so that, apart from an action plan for haze, we will also have action plans for floods and droughts,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) on the government’s measures in the event of a severe drought or El Nino, including identifying high-risk areas and coordinating efforts among departments, while winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 (Budget 2027) at the policy stage, for his ministry.
Earlier, Arthur said that, based on current projections, the strong El Nino phenomenon was expected to intensify to the very strong category between November 2026 and January 2027, and could persist until May 2027.
He added that the phenomenon could bring drier weather and extreme heat between January and May 2027, with maximum temperatures potentially reaching 40 degrees Celsius, particularly in the northern and interior parts of the Peninsula, as well as several interior areas of Sabah and Sarawak.
He said reduced rainfall was also expected, particularly between January and March 2027, with potentially more significant effects in the northern part of the Peninsula and Sabah.
In another development, Arthur said the implementation of a carbon tax should be carried out carefully and in stages, once the Climate Change Bill and the Climate Change Authority Bill were passed and gazetted, and their implementation frameworks were operating effectively.
Industry readiness must be taken into account to ensure that the transition to a low-carbon economy would not affect the country’s economic growth.
“NRES continues to provide cooperation and technical input to the Finance Ministry, to ensure that the implementation of any carbon pricing instruments is in line with the country’s climate change policies and commitments,” he said.
Meanwhile, on the issue of transboundary haze, he said that the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP) did not currently provide for a specific mechanism for compensation claims between countries.
However, Arthur said the government was open to examining the suitability of other legal mechanisms for compensation and damages, subject to the availability of a legal basis under international law.
“In this regard, a comprehensive study of the economic losses caused by haze, including its effects on public health, productivity and economic activity, is important as a scientific and economic basis for policy consideration and follow-up action,” he said.
Proposals for financial assistance to affected people, particularly gig workers, and the establishment of a haze disaster fund, required further study with the relevant ministries and agencies, taking into account existing assistance mechanisms, actual needs and the government’s financial implications.
The government would also continue to strengthen enforcement cooperation through bilateral and Asean channels, including by promoting the implementation of the polluter pays principle, he said. — Bernama

Title: Court of Appeal upholds Perak businessman’s acquittal on 122 cheating, forgery charges in RM6m case
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — The Court of Appeal today upheld the acquittal of a businessman on 122 counts of cheating and using forged documents involving medical equipment supply investments worth more than RM6 million in 2015.
A three-member panel comprising Justices Datuk Azman Abdullah, Datuk Hayatul Akmal Abdul Aziz, and K. Muniandy dismissed the prosecution’s final appeal against the acquittal of N. Narendran, 46, by the Ipoh High Court in January 2022.
Delivering the unanimous decision, Justice Muniandy said the bench was satisfied that the High Court judicial commissioner had correctly evaluated the burden of proof and applicable legal principles.
He said the absence of mens rea at the onset of the transactions, material contradictions in the charges, and the lack of forensic evidence proving forgery rendered the original Sessions Court conviction unsafe.
“We also found that the High Court judicial commissioner did not commit any error of fact or law warranting appellate intervention. On the contrary, the High Court correctly identified fatal fundamental flaws in the prosecution’s case, rendering the Sessions Court’s conviction unsafe to uphold,” he said.
“The appellant’s appeal is therefore unanimously dismissed. The High Court’s discharge and acquittal order for the respondent (Narendran) on all 122 charges is valid and affirmed,” he added.
Justice Muniandy noted that because the forgery charges were inextricably linked to the primary cheating allegations that the prosecution failed to prove, the charges under Section 471 of the Penal Code collapsed on their own.
On April 9, 2021, the Ipoh Sessions Court sentenced Narendran to 10 years’ imprisonment and 24 strokes of the cane after finding him guilty of all charges. The High Court subsequently overturned the conviction and acquitted him in January 2022 following his appeal.
According to the charge sheet, Narendran faced 105 counts of cheating a man by deceiving him into believing that state government purchase orders for investments in supplying disposable medical equipment to a hospital in Ipoh, Perak, were genuine.
He was accused of inducing the victim to hand over cheques and cash amounting to between RM20,000 and RM350,000 for non-existent investments at four locations between May and December 2015.
The charges were framed under Section 420 of the Penal Code, which provides for a prison sentence of up to 10 years, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
Narendran also faced 17 counts of using forged documents involving the same victim and transaction under Section 471 of the Penal Code, punishable under Section 467 of the same code, which carries a maximum jail term of 20 years and a fine.
He allegedly used several forged Perak state government purchase orders as genuine at Ganang Resources, No C-2-09, Persiaran Greentown 3, Greentown Business Centre, between April and October 2015.
Deputy Public Prosecutor How May Ling appeared for the prosecution, while counsel S. Meharaj, Nur Syazwani Hassan, and R. Vikraman represented Narendran. — Bernama

Title: The Selangor royal aide who wasn’t: Man nabbed over RM1.42m car and property scam
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 28 — Police have arrested a man suspected of being the mastermind behind a vehicle and property sale scam in which photographs of the Raja Muda of Selangor were allegedly misused, with total losses estimated at RM1.42 million.
Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the 40-year-old suspect was arrested in Johor Bahru at about 5 pm yesterday following continuous intelligence gathering into 26 police reports received nationwide since 2023.
“During the arrest, the suspect was found hiding at a residential property belonging to an acquaintance in Johor, which is believed to have served as his hideout after he went missing on October 13.
“Also arrested were two siblings who were acquaintances of the suspect — a 26-year-old woman in Shah Alam, followed by her 27-year-old brother in Johor Bahru — after they were suspected of conspiring to hide him,” he told a press conference at the Selangor police headquarters here today.
Shazeli said further investigations found that the suspect used the same modus operandi with each victim, posing as an aide-de-camp to the Raja Muda of Selangor before offering properties of various categories and vehicles for sale.
He said investigations also found that the self-employed suspect had no affiliation with or official appointment at any palace or the Selangor royal institution.
“In Selangor alone, 15 police reports have been lodged, involving losses amounting to RM960,020. The suspect is believed to have been active since 2023, with victims also reported outside Selangor, including in Kuala Lumpur, Kedah, Perak, Negeri Sembilan and Perlis.
“Police are now applying for remand orders for all the suspects under Section 420 of the Penal Code to assist in investigations. The case is still being investigated in detail to determine whether any remaining members of the group or accomplices are still at large,” he said.
In a separate development, Shazeli said the Selangor Commercial Crime Investigation Department had dismantled online scam syndicates with the arrest of 58 individuals in raids conducted from October 20 to 26.
“All those arrested, aged between 20 and 50, comprised eight local men and 50 foreign nationals — 45 men and five women — most of whom originated from East Asia.
“Cross-checks are being conducted with the Immigration Department to verify their documents, and preliminary investigations found that all had entered the country through legal entry points,” he said.
He said all the suspects worked as customer service operators involved in investment scams, love scams and fake job offers, targeting victims overseas, including in Europe and East Asia, since August.
Shazeli said police also seized various communication devices worth RM228,000 during the operation, including 117 mobile phones, 21 desktop computers, 16 laptops, eight routers or modems, two iPads and two central processing units.
All the suspects have been remanded under Sections 420 and 120B of the Penal Code, with varying remand periods. — Bernama

Title: Severe storm alert: MetMalaysia warns of heavy rain across KL, Selangor and eight states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning across several states and federal territories, forecasting heavy rain and strong winds until 8pm today.
In an advisory released at 4.15pm, the department cautioned that the alert covers the entirety of Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, and Melaka.
In Selangor, the affected districts comprise Hulu Langat, Gombak, Sepang, Petaling, and Hulu Selangor.
Other peninsular locations on alert include Perak (Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, and Muallim), Pahang (Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Jerantut, and Raub), Negeri Sembilan (Seremban, Rembau, Port Dickson, and Jelebu), and Johor (Batu Pahat, Kluang, Kota Tinggi, Johor Bahru, Pontian, and Kulai).
Across Sarawak, bad weather is forecast for Samarahan (Sebuyau), Sri Aman, Bintulu (Tatau), Kapit (Song), Sibu, Mukah, Betong, Sarikei, Limbang, and Miri (Marudi).
In Sabah, the warning applies to the interior districts of Pensiangan and Tambunan, the West Coast areas of Ranau and Kota Belud, Sandakan, and Kota Marudu in Kudat.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings when radar indicators show precipitation exceeding 20mm per hour that is either imminent or expected to persist for over an hour. These advisories serve as short-term alerts, valid for a maximum of six hours from issuance.

Title: Fewer foreign workers, more jobs for Malaysians: DPM Zahid outlines government’s priorities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The government will continue implementing measures to gradually reduce the country’s reliance on foreign workers, in line with the direction set out in the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP), said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
In a Facebook post today, Ahmad Zahid, who is also rural and regional development minister, said the efforts would take into account the actual needs of industries while prioritising employment opportunities for Malaysians.
“I have also reviewed feedback from all ministries and agencies involved in the employment of foreign workers.
“We have agreed on the need for collective decision-making to address issues and challenges in managing the quota mechanism and ceiling for the employment of foreign workers, while ensuring that job opportunities for Malaysians remain our top priority,” he said in the post.
Ahmad Zahid said he had highlighted the matter while chairing the third Cabinet Committee Meeting on Foreign Workers at Parliament today.
He added that the government would continue to ensure that every policy implemented could strengthen employment opportunities for Malaysians while supporting industry needs and benefiting the people as a whole. — Bernama

Title: MACC monitoring over, but HRD Corp must now show results from RM2b training levies, says MEF
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has called on the Human Resource Development Corporation (HRD Corp) to prioritise skills development, training quality and measurable workplace outcomes following the conclusion of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) governance monitoring of the agency.
MEF Senior Advisor for Government, Media and International Engagement Datuk Syed Hussain Syed Husman said the conclusion of the monitoring marked an important step towards restoring employers’ confidence in HRD Corp following the implementation of governance improvement measures.
He commended Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and HRD Corp chief executive officer Datuk Shamir Abdul Aziz for their efforts to address governance concerns raised by the authorities, but stressed that the reform process must continue.
“The conclusion of MACC’s governance monitoring is a positive development. However, this should not be seen as the end of the reform process. It must mark the beginning of a stronger phase of performance, accountability and results,” he said in a statement today.
Syed Hussain said HRD Corp, which manages levy collections of approximately RM2 billion, should move beyond measuring success based on the amount of levy collected or the number of training programmes conducted.
Instead, he said, the agency should focus on equipping businesses with the skills they need, improving workers’ competencies and productivity, and ensuring that training investments generate measurable returns.
He added that training programmes must also keep pace with current and emerging industry requirements, particularly in artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, automation, green technology and Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET).
MEF also called for stricter accreditation standards and regular performance assessments of training providers, with evaluations based on employer feedback, improvements in participants’ competencies and actual workplace outcomes.
To improve accessibility, particularly for small and medium enterprises (SMEs), Syed Hussain said HRD Corp should streamline course registration, training approvals and claims processing through digitalisation, while maintaining transparency and effective financial controls.
He also urged the agency to strengthen internal governance, publish meaningful key performance indicators (KPIs), improve fund management transparency, and enhance its research and risk assessment capabilities.
“Malaysia cannot afford a training system that is focused on processes but falls short on outcomes. Every ringgit invested in workforce development must deliver value,” he said.
Syed Hussain said MEF was ready to work with HRD Corp and the Human Resources Ministry to ensure workforce development investments delivered meaningful and measurable benefits to businesses, workers and the nation. — Bernama

Title: Who’s behind the haze? No conclusive evidence linking Malaysian firms to Indonesia fires, says Arthur Kurup
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — There is no conclusive evidence that Malaysian-linked plantation companies were responsible for fires in Indonesia, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said.
He said NRES and the Plantation and Commodities Ministry had examined allegations that Malaysian companies were involved in burning activities in Indonesia.
“Based on our assessment to date, there is no conclusive evidence confirming that Malaysian-linked plantation companies were responsible for the fires.
“The government’s position is clear that any party proven to be responsible for haze pollution must face appropriate action in accordance with the law,” he said.
Arthur was winding up the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for his ministry in the Dewan Rakyat today. He was responding to Mohamad Shafizan Kepli (GPS-Batang Lupar), who asked about proposals for specific legislation to address transboundary haze pollution and action against companies found responsible.
Arthur said the proposal to restrict financing for companies proven to be responsible for haze pollution required further scrutiny, particularly regarding the legal basis, evidentiary standards, jurisdiction and implications for the financial sector.
“The ministry has also examined on several occasions the merits of enacting a Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, similar to legislation introduced by a neighbouring country.
“However, implementation would present challenges, particularly in terms of jurisdiction, the collection and verification of evidence overseas, the determination of corporate liability and the implications for the sovereignty of other countries,” he said.
On proposals to seek compensation and damages, Arthur said the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP) did not currently provide a specific mechanism for compensation claims between countries.
“Nevertheless, the government is open to examining the suitability of other legal mechanisms, subject to the availability of a basis under international law.
“A comprehensive study of the economic losses caused by haze, including its effects on public health, productivity and economic activity, is important in providing a scientific and economic basis for policy considerations and follow-up action,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘All is well, kita Geng Biru’: Zahid signals unity after meeting MCA’s Wee Ka Siong amid Melaka seat row
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir met MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong at the Parliament building today, believed to be over seat allocation ahead of the Melaka state election.
The three leaders were seen entering the Members of Parliament Block at about 12.20pm amid a dispute over the announcement of BN candidates for the polls.
Meanwhile, Ahmad Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister, uploaded a photograph of himself with the two leaders on Facebook, accompanied by a brief caption suggesting a positive outcome from the meeting.
“Don’t worry. All is well.
Kita Geng Biru
(We are the Blue Gang),” he wrote in the post.
However, as of now, there has been no official confirmation of the matters discussed or any decisions reached during the meeting.
MCA leaders are also understood to be scheduled to hold a meeting at Wisma MCA this afternoon following the meeting.
At the BN candidate announcement ceremony for the Melaka state election in Ayer Keroh on October 24, Wee had questioned the event, claiming that it was held without MCA’s consent. He also stressed that MCA did not recognise the announcement as the party had not agreed to the list of candidates announced. — Bernama

Title: Botched Pahang raid leaves member of public injured, National Anti-Drugs Agency considers body cameras for officers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) will discuss with the Home Ministry (KDN) a proposal to seek funding from the Finance Ministry for the procurement of body cameras for its enforcement officers.
Its director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the move followed a recommendation by the Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission (EAIC) for KDN to prioritise the provision of body cameras for AADK officers conducting field operations.
In a statement today, he said AADK remained committed to ensuring that all enforcement operations were conducted responsibly, transparently and in compliance with the law and human rights, in the interest of public safety and order.
He added that the agency would improve its risk assessment guidelines for operations and ensure that enforcement officers complied with logbook requirements without exception.
AADK would also take follow-up action, including disciplinary measures against officers found to have been negligent or to have breached standard operating procedures (SOPs) during an enforcement operation in Bera, Pahang, on October 13 last year.
Yesterday, the EAIC recommended that KDN prioritise the provision of body cameras for AADK enforcement personnel following an incident during an operation to locate a suspected individual in Bera last year.
The commission said its investigation found negligence in the tactical handling of the raid and non-compliance with SOPs by the Bera AADK operations team, which triggered panic and a scuffle that resulted in injuries to a member of the public or a third party at the scene. — Bernama

Title: Family apologises to Bella Astillah over Muar woman’s viral grab-and-kiss incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The family of a wedding guest who went viral for grabbing Bella Astillah by the back of her neck to kiss her on the cheek has publicly apologised to the singer-actress.
The woman’s daughter-in-law phoned in to ERA radio station’s 3 Pagi ERA segment to tender the apology after previous attempts to reach Bella through Instagram direct messages went unanswered,
Berita Harian
reported.
“My entire family would like to apologise for my mother’s excitement. I am truly sorry, as what happened was beyond our expectations. We never expected this to happen,” she said.
“Our whole family tried sending Bella direct messages on Instagram, but there was no response. So, when I happened to see Bella, I immediately called her,” she said in a video posted on Instagram.
Taking the situation in stride, Bella assured listeners that she was unhurt and thanked the caller for making the effort to reach out.
The 32-year-old also apologised on behalf of her fans, acknowledging that intense public backlash online might have hurt the family’s feelings.
“That’s okay. I’m the person involved, and I’m fine. There’s no problem and I haven’t suffered any injuries. On behalf of Bella, I would also like to apologise if some fans were overly concerned and caused your mother-in-law to go viral. I’m sorry about that too.
“Thank you for taking the time to contact me. But don’t worry, from my side, everything is fine. These things happen unexpectedly.
“At the same time, Bella is actually perfectly fine and has not suffered any injuries. Please send my regards to your mother-in-law. Hopefully, we’ll get to meet again, God willing,” she said.
The incident occurred during a
kenduri rakyat
at Yong Sheng Banquet Hall on Jalan Bakri in Muar last Sunday, where more than 10,000 guests turned up to celebrate Bella, whose real name is Dayang Nabellah Awang Astillah, and her husband, Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman, 33.
A viral video of the greeting line showed the woman suddenly grabbing Bella by the nape of her neck and pulling her in close for a kiss, catching the bride visibly off guard and sparking widespread discussion on the internet.
The couple solemnised their marriage in a private ceremony on 10 October before hosting a grand reception at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre in Kuala Lumpur on October 18.
Their wedding tour concludes with another
kenduri rakyat i
n Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, on October 31 .

Title: KLIA Customs seizes RM49.5m in AI chips with potential military uses, fifth case in RM100m syndicate probe
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 28 — The Customs Department at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) foiled an attempt to transit 30 servers containing advanced artificial intelligence (AI) chips worth nearly RM49.5 million without the required authorisation.
The chips could potentially be used in the development of military technology.
KLIA Customs director Aspalila Ag. Tuah said the seizure was made by a team from the KLIA Customs Enforcement Division following a thorough inspection of a warehouse in the KLIA Free Trade Zone on October 15 at about 11.30am.
She said preliminary investigations found that the servers had been brought in from an Asian country under a single air waybill declaring them as electronic components, allegedly to evade detection by the authorities, before being re-exported to another Asian country.
“The syndicate also used Malaysia as a transit point to ensure there were no restrictions on the export of the servers to their next destination,” she told a press conference here today.
Meanwhile, Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) Strategic Trade Secretariat senior assistant director Masyita Ismail said the high-performance AI chips were subject to strict controls as they were classified as dual-use items.
“The Strategic Trade Act 2010 regulates dual-use items, which can be used in the development of weapons of mass destruction,” she said, adding that the brands, countries of origin and destinations of the chips could not be disclosed as investigations were ongoing.
Miti enforces Strategic Trade Controller’s Directive No. 1/2025 to regulate the export, transit and transhipment of advanced AI chips in Malaysia, with the aim of preventing the country from being used as a transit hub for high-performance chips destined for sanctioned countries.
The directive stipulates that chips with a Total Processing Performance (TPP) value of 4,800 or higher, or 1,600 or higher when combined with a Performance Density of 3.2 or higher, require a permit, which must be applied for 30 days before the chips are brought into Malaysia.
Aspalila confirmed that the seizure was the fifth case involving the same syndicate recorded by Customs this year, with the total value of seizures across all five cases exceeding RM100 million.
She said companies handling the shipments had been called in to assist investigations, but no arrests had been made so far.
All the cases are being investigated under Section 12 of the Strategic Trade Act 2010, which provides for a fine of up to RM20 million for a corporation, or a fine of up to RM10 million, imprisonment for up to 10 years, or both, for an individual convicted of an offence committed wilfully. — Bernama

Title: Behind Chow Kit shopfronts, Immigration uncovers alleged illegal money transfer network, eight detained
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 28 — An illegal money transfer syndicate using the ‘Hundi’ system and targeting Bangladeshi nationals in the Klang Valley was uncovered after the Immigration Department raided three premises in Chow Kit yesterday, where the activities were being conducted under the guise of retail and wholesale businesses.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the special operation, which began at 2.37pm, led to the arrest of eight Bangladeshi men aged between 24 and 42 following a month of intelligence gathering.
He said the syndicate was believed to have used retail and wholesale business premises as a front to evade detection by the authorities.
“The syndicate is believed to have targeted Bangladeshi nationals in the Klang Valley by using e-wallet accounts and local bank accounts registered under the names of foreign agents to conduct financial transactions.
“For customers without access to digital accounts, money was received and sent in cash,” he said in a statement here today.
Zakaria said investigations also found that the syndicate’s agents operated according to Bangladesh’s banking hours, from Sunday to Thursday, between noon and 8 pm local time.
“Further checks found that transactions recorded in the e-wallet accounts from January to October 2026 amounted to more than RM180,000,” he said.
Zakaria said enforcement officers also seized RM24,720 in cash believed to be proceeds from the activities, as well as five Bangladeshi passports, five mobile phones, a laptop, closed-circuit television (CCTV) equipment, QR codes and several business documents.
He said the seized documents included copies of documents from the Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM), Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) licences, shop stamps and premises keys.
Zakaria said preliminary checks found that two of the eight Bangladeshi nationals detained had overstayed in the country, while the other six were believed to have misused their respective immigration passes.
All eight were detained on suspicion of committing offences under Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963 before being taken to the Immigration Office for further investigation.
He said two other Bangladeshi men, as well as a local man and a local woman, were also issued notices to appear at the Immigration office to assist in the investigation.
The operation was carried out by the Intelligence and Special Operations Division of the Immigration Department headquarters in Putrajaya, in collaboration with the National Anti-Financial Crime Centre (NFCC). — Bernama

Title: KLIA Customs seizes RM1m in cannabis and ketamine hidden in shoes, toys and tool shipments
Article:
SEPANG, Oct 28 — The Royal Malaysian Customs Department at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) has foiled two attempts to smuggle cannabis flowers and ketamine weighing a total of 16.39kg and worth RM1.03 million.
KLIA Customs director Aspalila Ag. Tuah said the first case involved the seizure of seven packages containing 7.28kg of cannabis flowers worth RM582,400 at the Pos Malaysia International Mail Centre at KLIA on October 12. The drugs were believed to be destined for export to a European country.
“KLIA Customs found airtight transparent plastic packages suspected to contain cannabis flowers hidden in boxes declared as containing shoes and toys,” she told a press conference here today.
In the second case, an enforcement team seized a box containing nine aluminium packets filled with 9.114kg of ketamine, worth RM455,700, at a cargo terminal in the KLIA Free Trade Zone on October 9, she said.
“The drugs were brought in through cargo services and concealed in aluminium packets and boxes declared as containing pipe wrenches and toolboxes to avoid detection by the authorities,” she said, adding that the consignment from a European country was believed to be destined for Kuala Lumpur.
She said both cases, which are being investigated under Section 39B(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952, involved shipments with incomplete and false recipient and sender addresses.
In another development, Aspalila said two Mini Cooper S cars worth an estimated RM180,000 were seized at two locations in Sepang on September 14 for being smuggled into the country without valid import permits and fitted with false registration numbers to evade detection, with the estimated taxes and duties totalling RM154,620.
“Efforts are underway to trace the vehicle owners, and the cases are being investigated under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967,” she said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia to introduce new rules on AI use in court within next few weeks, says Chief Justice
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 28 — The judiciary will issue a new practice direction on the use of artificial intelligence (AI) by lawyers and court officers in legal proceedings within the next few weeks, says Chief Justice (CJ) Tun Wan Ahmad Farid Wan Salleh.
He said the move came amid concerns over the reliability of AI-generated legal submissions, which could appear convincing despite containing inaccurate information.
“Today, AI can produce submissions that look polished and persuasive, but entirely wrong. On our part, we will issue a practice direction in a few weeks in respect of the usage of AI in legal proceedings,” he said in his keynote address at the International Malaysia Law Conference 2026 here today.
Wan Ahmad Farid stressed that while technology could help accelerate the administration of justice, it should never replace human judgment, particularly when courts are required to exercise judicial discretion.
“Technology can accelerate the administration of justice, but it can never become the author of justice itself. The duty belongs exclusively to us, human custodians of the law,” he said.
Wan Ahmad Farid cited Malaysia’s 2023 reforms abolishing the mandatory death penalty, which allowed judges to consider the circumstances of individual cases instead of being bound by a mandatory death sentence, as an example of the importance of judicial discretion in ensuring fairness.
He noted that said technology could not replicate the human considerations involved in administering justice, particularly when balancing the rights of accused persons with the interests of victims.
“No computer programme can look into the eyes of a victim and offer vindication, nor can it look at an accused person and temper justice with mercy,” he said.
The CJ also reminded judges and legal practitioners of the importance of intellectual honesty, particularly as technology continued to transform the legal profession.
For judges, he said, this meant ensuring that judgments reflected a proper appreciation of the facts and law, including addressing arguments that challenged their conclusions.
Lawyers, meanwhile, must ensure that legal authorities were cited accurately and that clients were given honest advice, particularly when the legal position remained uncertain.
Wan Ahmad Farid said judges must decide cases based on the law and evidence without yielding to public pressure or external influence.
Speaking to reporters, the top judge said that the new practice direction would apply to legal practitioners and court officers, while judges already had their own guidelines governing the use of AI.
“We are not going to discourage them. We are encouraging them, but there has to be a guideline for them to follow. It could help expedite court proceedings and save valuable time for judges and lawyers, provided the technology is used responsibly,” he said.
However, he cautioned against excessive reliance on AI, which could undermine human reasoning and critical thinking. — Bernama

Title: RM1m to look the other way? Two enforcement officers among five nabbed in Johor MACC foreign worker graft probe
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 28 — The Johor Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has remanded five individuals, including two federal enforcement agency officers, on suspicion of soliciting and receiving about RM1 million in bribes from a foreign worker agency.
Johor MACC director Datuk Hazrul Shazreen Abd Yazid said a five-day remand order until November 1 was issued by Magistrate A. Dhilip Nair at the Johor Bahru Court Complex here today, after allowing an application by the commission.
He said the other three individuals detained were foreign worker agents.
“The five suspects, comprising three men and two women, aged between their 40s and 60s, were detained between 10am and 4pm yesterday in operations conducted in Selangor and Johor.
“Preliminary investigations found that all the suspects were believed to have conspired to solicit and receive bribes in return for not taking enforcement action against foreign workers under the agency’s supervision,” he said in a statement today.
Hazrul Shazreen said the alleged offences were believed to have been committed between 2018 and 2025, involving 44 online money transfers totalling about RM1 million during that period.
He said the case was being investigated under Sections 16(a)(B) and 16(b)(B) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009, following an operation conducted by the MACC Intelligence Division. — Bernama
